question.text: What percentage of companies globally will fulfill their pre-2026 broiler commitments in 2026 and 2027?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage of global companies reporting in 2026 or 2027 that they have fulfilled the broiler commitments they made before 2026 according to [Chicken Watch](https://chickenwatch.org/progress-tracker) when accessed by Metaculus on January 1, 2028.
question.fine_print:
Specifically, the denominator will be obtained by selecting the "Broiler" issue on the [Chicken Watch](https://chickenwatch.org/progress-tracker?filterK=Cage-free) progress tracker, a "Victory Date" of 1990 to 2025, and a "Timeline" of 2026 and after. The numerator will then be obtained by *additionally* selecting the "Reporting Fulfilled" status.

If Chicken Watch ceases reporting or significantly changes its criteria such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question will be **annulled**.

# Chicken Watch broiler commitments: what share is reported as fulfilled (research notes, 2026-11-05)

I could not read the resolution number directly. The Chicken Watch tracker builds its counts in the browser, so my fetch tool only saw the page text, not the figures. The current numerator and denominator need to be checked by hand on the live tracker.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05: I fetched https://chickenwatch.org/progress-tracker?filterK=Broiler, a version with a "Reporting Fulfilled" filter, and /broiler. None of them showed counts for commitments, statuses, Victory Date or Timeline. The /broiler page only lists example companies (Kraft Heinz, Subway, Campbell's, Royal Caribbean, Carnival, Accor, Nestlé) and the figure of about 70 billion chickens raised for meat each year. A guessed data address (/api/progress-tracker) returned a 404 error. [Chicken Watch](https://chickenwatch.org/progress-tracker?filterK=Broiler), [Broiler page](https://chickenwatch.org/broiler)
- Inference, not confirmed: the question's range of 0.862068965645% to 14.9014778321% matches 7/812 and 121/812 exactly. So when the question was written, the filtered denominator was probably 812 commitments, with the bounds set at 7 and 121 fulfilled. The lower bound may be close to the count at that time. Please check this on the live site.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Most broiler commitments, especially Better Chicken Commitment (BCC) pledges, had a 2026 deadline. Companies are only now reporting on them, and the numerator can still grow through 2027.
- An older forum post said Chicken Watch listed 1,672 broiler commitments, 1,007 of them due between 2020 and 2026. [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/oRFgCTNKZirQyFzPT/corporate-commitments-breakdown)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Albert Schweitzer Stiftung published its Masthuhn-Report 2026 (Germany, more than 60 companies):
  - About 70% of companies have committed, but only about 20% of the required progress has been made.
  - Only Yorma's and 60 seconds to Napoli score 100%. Hans im Glück finished implementation by the end of 2024.
  - Nestlé, Rügenwalder Mühle and Genuss & Harmonie withdrew their pledges. McDonald's and Burger King score 0%.
  - Dr. Oetker scores 88%. No supermarket or discounter reaches 60%; Aldi Süd is highest at 54%.
  [topagrar](https://www.topagrar.com/gefluegel/tierschutzer-beklagen-schleppende-fortschritte-bei-hahnchenhaltung-20030744.html), [SWR](https://www.swr.de/leben/verbraucher/tierwohl-in-der-huehnermast-wie-weit-sind-lebenmittel-hersteller-supermaerkte-und-burger-ketten-100.html), [news38](https://www.news38.de/panorama/verbraucher/article300717509/masthuhn-report-2026-aldi-lidl-discounter.html)
- 2026-03 (per search summaries): the European ChickenTrack 2025 report from Compassion in World Farming (CIWF) said Waitrose and REMA 1000 Norge reached full BCC compliance, joining Norsk Kylling (fully compliant since 2022). 76 of 107 companies reported progress, up from 64 of 93. CIWF criticised UK hospitality firms for "stepping back" from their commitments. [Provisioner](https://www.provisioneronline.com/articles/116676-chickentrack-report-highlights-better-chicken-commitment-progress), [Retail Insight Network](https://www.retail-insight-network.com/newsletters/european-hotels-and-retailers-advance-on-chicken-welfare-commitments), [FDBusiness](https://www.fdbusiness.com/chickentrack-2025-shows-steady-progress-on-broiler-welfare-but-calls-for-continued-industry-commitment/)
- Undated (2025/26): KFC said it would not meet its 2026 BCC pledge on slower-growing breeds. [Poultry World](https://www.poultryworld.net/the-industrymarkets/market-trends-analysis-the-industrymarkets-2/better-chicken-commitment-reveals-limited-progress-ahead-of-2026-deadline/) (the page returned a 403 error, so this comes from the search snippet)
- The Humane League projected that about 28% of UK chicken supply would be BCC-compliant by the end of 2026. [THL](https://thehumaneleague.org/article/measuring-bcc-compliant-chicken-supply)

## 4. Base rates
- 2023-04: in the first European ChickenTrack, 42 commitments (58%) were not reporting any progress. 12 commitments (16%) reported 100% compliance with at least one criterion, which is not the same as full fulfilment. [CIWF](https://ciwf.org/media-news/latest-news/2023/04/first-european-chickentrack-report-launched)
- 2022-2023: in the US ChickenTrack, about 18% of more than 230 committed companies reported progress in 2022, and 22% of 52 tracked companies reported publicly in 2023. [CIWF 2022 PDF](https://www.ciwf.com/media/7453487/chickentrack-2022.pdf)
- Full broiler fulfilment has been rare: only a few companies are confirmed worldwide (Norsk Kylling, Waitrose, REMA 1000, some small German restaurant chains). By contrast, about 92% of cage-free egg commitments with past deadlines reportedly showed some progress by July 2025 (title of an EA Forum post I could not open because of a 429 error). [EA Forum](https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/HwXBSEgaXvyhLixxL/as-of-july-2025-92-of-cage-free-egg-commitments-with)
- Trend: reporting is slowly increasing, withdrawals are happening, and full fulfilment stays in the low single-digit percentages.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets supplied match this question; they cover broiler production volumes, chicken menu prices and so on.
- An older Metaculus question on the number of broiler pledges resolved at 615 on 2023-12-01. It is a count of pledges, not fulfilment. [Manifold mirror](https://manifold.markets/MetaculusBot/on-december-1st-2023-how-many-compa)
- I could not find the Metaculus community forecast for this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The 2026 BCC deadline passes. Companies' sustainability reports and responses to Chicken Watch in late 2026 and 2027 should add fulfilment claims.
- The next European ChickenTrack is expected around March 2027, plus any US ChickenTrack and the Open Wing Alliance's broiler reporting.
- More withdrawals (like Nestlé and Rügenwalder in Germany) or deadline extensions (like KFC) could hold the numerator down. Whether Chicken Watch drops withdrawn commitments or reclassifies them would also change the denominator.
- Annulment risk: the question is annulled if Chicken Watch changes its methodology.

## Chicken Watch broiler fulfillment rate: research brief (as of 2026-11-05)

Main limitation: I couldn't get the live figures from the resolution source. The Chicken Watch tracker builds its numbers in the browser, so my fetches only returned the page shell: no counts, filters or statuses. A guessed API address (chickenwatch.org/api/commitments) returned 404. The current numerator and denominator need to be checked by hand in a browser.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-05: I fetched https://chickenwatch.org/progress-tracker?filterK=Broiler. It showed no company counts, statuses or data, only site links and a 2026 copyright. [Chicken Watch](https://chickenwatch.org/progress-tracker?filterK=Broiler)
- 2026-11-05: The broiler page (chickenwatch.org/broiler) has no statistics either. It shows example logos (Kraft Heinz, Subway, Campbell's, Royal Caribbean, Carnival, Accor, Nestlé) and links to the tracker. [Chicken Watch broiler](https://chickenwatch.org/broiler)
- The question's range (0.86% to 14.9%) hints that the current share is low, probably in the low single digits. That is my inference from the range, not something I verified.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The Chicken Watch tracker is the only thing that counts, and only as it reads on 2028-01-01. Most broiler pledges (Better Chicken Commitment, BCC) had a 2026 deadline, so companies may self-report fulfillment during 2026 and 2027. Evidence from 2025-2026 says few companies are fully compliant.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Albert Schweitzer Stiftung's Masthuhn-Report 2026 rated over 60 companies in Germany. About 70% have broiler pledges, but only about 20% of the required progress has been made. All 17 supermarkets and discounters scored below 60%. Aldi Süd leads; Lidl and Nestlé lag. [SWR](https://www.swr.de/leben/verbraucher/tierwohl-in-der-huehnermast-wie-weit-sind-lebenmittel-hersteller-supermaerkte-und-burger-ketten-100.html), [topagrar](https://www.topagrar.com/gefluegel/tierschutzer-beklagen-schleppende-fortschritte-bei-hahnchenhaltung-20030744.html), [news38](https://www.news38.de/panorama/verbraucher/article300717509/masthuhn-report-2026-aldi-lidl-discounter.html)
- 2026-08 (per search summary): The Humane League UK reported that KFC and Popeyes had not rejoined the BCC. Dave's Hot Chicken is the only chain in that group still committed. [Farm Change](https://farmchange.substack.com/p/uk-brands-including-burger-king-kfc)
- 2026-02-19: Eight businesses owning 18 UK hospitality brands (Burger King, KFC, Nando's, The Restaurant Group and others) dropped the BCC for the industry-led Sustainable Chicken Forum, which does not require slower-growing breeds. If Chicken Watch marks these as withdrawn or removes them, the denominator could change. [The Ecologist](https://theecologist.org/2026/feb/19/food-brands-break-frankenchickens-promise), [World Animal Protection](https://www.worldanimalprotection.org.uk/latest/blogs/better-chicken-commitment-dropped/), [FarmingUK](https://www.farminguk.com/news/fast-growing-breed-row-erupts-after-firms-quit-better-chicken-commitment_68043.html)
- 2025-09-01: Waitrose said all its own-brand chicken now meets the BCC. M&S says it will be fully compliant across all chicken by the end of 2026. [search summary; The Grocer](https://www.thegrocer.co.uk/news/uk-food-businesses-unlikely-to-meet-2026-chicken-welfare-deadline/702371.article)

### 4. Base rates
- 2025-03: ChickenTrack 2025 (Compassion in World Farming's annual European report) covered 107 companies. 76 reported progress (71%, up from 69%). Only Waitrose and REMA 1000 Norge were fully BCC compliant, plus Norsk Kylling (since 2022): about 3 of 107, or roughly 3%. [Ethical Marketing News](https://ethicalmarketingnews.com/chickentrack-2025-shows-steady-progress-on-broiler-welfare-but-calls-for-continued-industry-commitment)
- 2024-03: In the US ChickenTrack (2023 data), 22% of North American BCC signatories reported any progress. The 2022 data showed 18% of 230+ companies. [CIWF](https://ciwf.com/media-and-news/news/2024/03/more-us-food-companies-share-progress-towards-adopting-higher-welfare-chicken)
- 2023: The European ChickenTrack (2022 data) found 4 of 73 companies (5%) reporting progress toward full BCC compliance. 16% reported 100% on at least one criterion. [CIWF 2022 report](https://www.ciwf.org/media/7453677/european-chickentrack-2022.pdf)
- Trend: reporting rates are rising slowly, but full fulfillment stays in the low single digits. The breed-change requirement shows the least progress. I didn't find a 2026 ChickenTrack edition, and I have no historical time series of the Chicken Watch "Reporting Fulfilled" share.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the pre-collected Kalshi or Polymarket markets match this question. They cover chicken menu prices, Arkansas broiler output and others, none relevant here.
- I found no Metaculus community figure for this specific question. Related Metaculus questions on Global Animal Partnership (GAP) broiler pledge counts exist (e.g., [Q3380](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/3380/when-will-at-least-750-companies-pledge-to-maintain-a-supply-chain-consistent-with-the-current-basic-global-animal-partnership-standards-for-broiler-chickens-by-end-of-2030)), but they measure something else.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- End of 2026: the BCC deadline passes. Companies may announce compliance, delays or withdrawals, and annual CSR and animal-welfare reports for 2026 come out in early to mid 2027.
- About March 2027: likely ChickenTrack 2027 (Europe and US), which feeds the self-reported data that trackers like Chicken Watch use.
- Possible further BCC withdrawals, like the UK Sustainable Chicken Forum moves, which could shrink or reclassify the denominator.
- If Chicken Watch changes its criteria or stops reporting, the question is annulled.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** Forecasts close on 2026-11-30, and the platform lists resolution around 2026-12-31. The background text, however, says Chicken Watch will be accessed on January 1, 2028. So between about 2 and 14 months of new reporting could count. The 2026 Better Chicken Commitment (BCC) deadline falls inside that window.

(b) **Latest known value:** I could not read it directly, because the tracker builds its counts in the browser. The question's bounds match fractions of 812 exactly: 0.985% is 8/812 and 14.78% is 120/812. The hard floor is stated at 0.985%. That implies the filtered denominator was about 812 commitments when the question was written, with at least 8 reported fulfilled, so roughly 1% (around 2025/2026).

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 1.0%.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** Full broiler fulfilment is very rare. Only a handful of companies are confirmed worldwide: Norsk Kylling, Waitrose, REMA 1000, and a few small German chains such as Yorma's, 60 seconds to Napoli and Hans im Glück. Chicken Watch updates statuses slowly. After the 2026 deadline, perhaps 5 to 20 more commitments get marked fulfilled, which would put the value at about 1.5% to 3.5%. The denominator may also shift through withdrawals or backfilled commitments.

(e) **Historical variation:** Broiler fulfilment counts have moved only by single digits per year. Reporting rates rise slowly, and full compliance stays in the low single-digit percentages.

(f) **Expert and market expectations:** There are no matching markets. Advocacy reports point to slow progress and some backsliding:
- The German Masthuhn-Report found only about 20% of the required implementation.
- KFC said it will miss its 2026 pledge.
- Nestlé and Rügenwalder Mühle withdrew their pledges in Germany.
- CIWF's European ChickenTrack shows rising reporting but few companies fully compliant.

(g) **Scenarios:**
- **Low:** Chicken Watch does not update broiler statuses at all, and new commitments are added to the denominator. The value stays at the floor of about 1%.
- **High:** After the deadline, Chicken Watch does a large batch update and marks many European restaurant chains and retailers, or partial-scope pledges, as fulfilled. The value could reach 6% to 10% or more.
- **Tails:** The 99th percentile reflects such a batch update. The 1st percentile is essentially the hard floor.

(b) **Latest known value:** I could not read the live tracker. That suggests about 7 to 8 commitments were "Reporting Fulfilled" at creation, around 0.9% to 1.0%.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about 1.0%.

(d) **If the current trend continued:**
- Full Better Chicken Commitment compliance remains rare. Confirmed cases include Waitrose, REMA 1000, Norsk Kylling and a few small German chains.

- Fulfilment claims after the 2026 deadline should trickle in during 2027, with a lag before Chicken Watch updates.

(e) **Historical variation:** The count of fully fulfilled broiler commitments has grown by only a handful per year. Changes to the denominator, such as reclassifying withdrawn commitments or adding new ones, could shift it by a few tenths of a percentage point.

(f) **Experts and markets:** No market matches this question. Animal welfare NGOs (CIWF, Albert Schweitzer Stiftung, The Humane League) report slow progress, with most companies far from full compliance and roughly 20% to 30% of the required progress made.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- Low: Chicken Watch is read at the end of 2026 with no updates, or it trims the denominator, leaving the figure at about 1%.
- High: Chicken Watch runs a bulk update after the deadline, logging many fulfilment self-reports (for example from European retailers, hospitality firms or smaller companies, possibly with partial criteria counted as fulfilled). That could push the count to 60 to 80 out of 812, or about 8% to 10%.
